newsitem.title: USA: U.S. forces set to evacuate Americans from Albania.
newsitem.headline: U.S. forces set to evacuate Americans from Albania.

text.p: U.S. forces in the Adriatic on Thursday were poised for a possible evacuation of Americans from Albania because of worsening instability in the small Balkan country.

White House spokesman David Johnson said U.S. policymakers were monitoring the situation closely, and that an evacuation was under active consideration "given the fact that it looks as though commercial flights have been suspended."
Defence Secretary William Cohen said the U.S. military is ready to begin the evacuation when and if needed.

"I think the situation in Albania is deteriorating and ... we will take whatever measures are necessary to make sure that those Americans who want to leave or need to leave will be safely evacuated so we are following it on a very close basis," Cohen, who was travelling in North Carolina with President Bill Clinton, told reporters.
"We have the capability and the capacity to provide for their evacuation and we will do so at the request of the ambassador," Cohen said.

Violence sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes has spread from southern Albania toward the capital of Tirana. International airline officials reported on Thursday that Tirana airport was closed, hampering the evacuation of some foreign embassy staff and families.
The U.S. State Department on Wednesday ordered 160 embassy employees and their dependents to leave by regular or charter flights. Another 2,000 Americans were urged to go.
Johnson said Americans were not a target in the spreading disorder, but simply faced a danger of "being in the wrong place at the wrong time."
The United States has powerful naval forces off the coast of Albania, including an aircraft carrier task force, which includes marine landing teams that would presumably carry out any evacuation.
A sign of deteriorating conditions in Albania occurred overnight when looters raided the military academy east of the capital and seized an unknown quantity of weapons.
Doctors reported five people had died in the northern city of Shkoder as looters seized arms from army depots there.
"This is a very dangerous situation. Ethnic tensions in the Balkans have long been a real problem for the entire world," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

McCurry said while economic problems were the immediate source of tension in the current crisis, Albania "fits into an ethnic equation in the Balkans that is part of a history there of conflict in the region."
The United States has nearly 8,000 troops in nearby Bosnia helping a NATO-led peacekeeping force police a peace agreement in the former Yugoslav region.
